docs.title: PFZL423Building latent world models for embodied decision-making.
docs.text:
Model-Based RL · Latent World Models · Embodied AI

Undergraduate student at Shanghai Jiao Tong University focusing on model-based reinforcement learning, latent world models, and embodied agents.

docs.title: Research Vision
docs.text:
I am interested in building latent world models that are useful not only for prediction, but also for planning, control, and cost-aware decision-making.

My long-term goal is to develop world models that are structurally aware of the planning problems they serve, enabling more efficient and robust embodied intelligence.

docs.title: Research Interests
docs.text:
• Latent Dynamics Models

    Learning compact world models optimized for control and planning.

  • Model-Based RL

    Using learned models to improve decision-making efficiency in embodied environments.

  • Cost-Aware Representation

    Connecting learned representations directly with downstream planning objectives and cost structures.

  • Embodied AI

    Studying agents that perceive, plan, and act through interaction with physical or simulated environments.

docs.title: CILD — Cost-Informed Latent Dynamics
docs.text:
CILD is an ongoing project built on top of TD-MPC2.

The project explores coupling representation learning with planner-aware cost heads. The objective is to ensure that latent dynamics models capture information that is most relevant for downstream control tasks.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: A living document tracking what I am learning, building, and reading. Updated periodically.

docs.title: Stage 1 — Motivation (current)
docs.text: Establish that current latent world models under-perform when representation learning and planning costs are treated as independent problems. Empirical study on dynamic-obstacle environments.

docs.title: Stage 2 — Method
docs.text: Develop CILD — a latent world model that couples representation learning with planner-aware cost heads (risk, progress, occupancy), trained jointly through the latent dynamics chain.

docs.title: Stage 3 — Planner
docs.text:
Build a cost-informed planner on top of CILD:

  • gradient-informed sampling
  • safety-constrained trajectory pruning
  • OOD-aware horizon adaptation

docs.title: Reading Standard
docs.text:
• For most papers: understand the main idea, run the code if available.
  • For core papers (DreamerV3, IRIS, SPR, TD-MPC2): read the code in detail; be able to explain the method to someone unfamiliar.
  • Always ask: can this be grafted onto the latent-dynamics framework to address a problem it currently cannot solve?

docs.title: Embodied AI
docs.text: Embodied AI studies agents that perceive, act, and learn through interaction with physical or simulated environments.

docs.title: My Current Understanding
docs.text: For me, Embodied AI is about connecting perception, world modeling, planning, and control.

docs.title: Questions
docs.text:
• What kind of world model is useful for action?
  • How should latent representations support planning?
  • How do costs and task structure shape learned dynamics?

docs.title: Latent World Models
docs.text: Latent world models learn compact representations of environment dynamics.

docs.title: Key Idea
docs.text: Instead of predicting raw observations directly, the model learns dynamics in a latent space that is hopefully useful for planning and control.

docs.title: My Focus
docs.text: I am especially interested in latent world models that are aware of the cost and planning structure of the task.

docs.title: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
docs.text: Model-based reinforcement learning uses a learned or known model of the environment to support planning and decision-making.

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text: For embodied agents, interaction can be expensive. A learned model can help the agent reason before acting.

docs.title: CILD — Cost-Informed Latent Dynamics
docs.text: CILD is an ongoing research project built on top of TD-MPC2.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
Many latent world models are optimized for prediction, but prediction alone may not be enough for planning.

CILD explores whether latent dynamics models can become more useful for control when they are trained with planner-aware cost information.

docs.title: Current Focus
docs.text:
• Latent dynamics modeling
  • Cost prediction in latent space
  • Planner-aware representation learning
  • TD-MPC2-style control

docs.text: Ongoing.
